candidate_findings.title: Central policy and Claude hooks both gate tools without an authority or failure contract
candidate_findings.claim: The central policy engine is declared the tool-governance authority, while provider hooks are also said to gate tools. The excerpt does not define which decision wins, whether hooks are advisory or enforcing, or what happens when a hook is absent, duplicated, times out, crashes, or disagrees with central policy.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A fail-open or divergent double-gate can execute a denied tool; a fail-closed or duplicate gate can deadlock execution or emit conflicting audit results.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define sole authorization authority, hook-to-policy decision mapping, fail-closed behavior, timeout/cancellation rules, idempotency keys, duplicate suppression, and normalized audit ordering.

evidence_refs.excerpt: Tools are governed by a central policy engine (permissions + validation + normalized tool results)
uses **Claude Code Hooks** (e.g., `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`) to gate tools and enrich telemetry.

candidate_findings.title: The thin-client command boundary lacks caller authentication and approval authority
candidate_findings.claim: Thin clients can start runs, approve tools, and cancel runs against a desktop-owned local server, but the bounded contract defines no authentication, pairing, authorization, transport protection, bind scope, revocation, CSRF/replay defense, or rule for which user may approve which run.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An unauthorized network or browser caller could influence execution or approve privileged tool activity through the desktop core even though direct provider/tool access is prohibited.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify bind/exposure policy, authenticated pairing, encrypted transport where non-loopback, caller/session identity, per-run authorization, approval freshness and scope, revocation, origin checks, replay protection, and auditable denial behavior.

evidence_refs.excerpt: desktop acts like a local server
command API (start run, approve tool, cancel run)
send command requests to the desktop-owned core only.

candidate_findings.title: The thin-client streaming and command APIs have no reconnect or delivery semantics
candidate_findings.claim: The proposed stable API boundary names streamed runs/events/artifacts and commands but does not define event sequence/cursors, ordering, replay windows, snapshot handoff, backpressure, command IDs, retry deduplication, acknowledgements, command results, or disconnect behavior.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Mobile/network retries can duplicate start/approve/cancel commands, miss events, display stale approval state, or overwhelm the desktop server, undermining the claimed deterministic event model.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define versioned envelopes, monotonic per-stream ordering, resume cursors and snapshot rules, bounded buffering/backpressure, idempotency keys and retention, acknowledgement/result states, cancellation races, and reconnect test oracles.

candidate_findings.title: Minimum attachment state cannot represent the required multiple viewers or enforce one writer
candidate_findings.claim: The contract requires multiple simultaneous read-only attachments, one mutation-capable focus holder, and tracked secondary attachments, but the minimum state exposes only scalar `attached_surface` and no attachment instance IDs, secondary collection, focus lease/version, or atomic transfer operation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two windows of the same surface kind cannot be distinguished, stale focus can route edits to the wrong window, and concurrent focus acquisition cannot be replayed or tested deterministically.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define attachment-instance identity and collection state, authoritative focus owner, atomic acquire/transfer/release with generation or compare-and-swap semantics, disconnect cleanup, denial UI, and concurrency tests.

candidate_findings.title: Default browser evidence has no sensitive-data, retention, or size contract
candidate_findings.claim: Browser evidence may include snapshots, screenshots, console/network summaries, and recordings/traces/videos, including around auth-session surfaces, but the excerpt provides no consent/default rule, redaction, secret classification, encryption/access control, retention/deletion, quotas, or capture backpressure.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Evidence can persist credentials, cookies, personal content, request bodies, and large recordings, causing privacy leakage and unbounded storage or performance degradation even though raw browser storage itself is excluded from `PreviewSession`.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define enablement and visible recording state, permission gates, URL/header/body/DOM redaction, secret scanning, encryption and access scope, retention/deletion, per-session size/time limits, backpressure/drop policy, and audit events.

candidate_findings.title: Credential identity propagation lacks an explicit secret-material exclusion

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A projector, event producer, health report, prompt assembler, or log summarizer could persist or index reusable secrets in seglog, redb, Tantivy, telemetry, or UI output.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Require secret-reference-only records, prohibit raw secrets in events/prompts/indexes/logs/runtime reports, define secure-store ownership, masking, rotation/revocation/deletion, error redaction, and deterministic secret-leak tests.

candidate_findings.title: First persist and artifact-to-document linking have no atomicity or conflict semantics
candidate_findings.claim: A transient generated buffer is authoritative until save/insert, first persist creates a path, and the artifact remains valid after linkage, but the contract does not define overwrite/conflict handling, concurrent saves, partial failure rollback, cancellation, revision advancement, or which representation is authoritative after linkage.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A crash or race can create an unlinked file, duplicate documents, divergent artifact and document content, unintended overwrite, or ambiguous restore behavior and audit history.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define one atomic save/link transaction with destination conflict policy, compare-against-source revision, cancellation boundary, rollback/recovery records, post-persist authority and resolver precedence, immutable audit lineage, and idempotent retry tests.
